Barbossa · Halloween campaign proposal

Noche de losMuertos

Saturday 31 October · Barbossa · From 10 PM

On Saturday 31 October, Barbossa hosts Noche de los Muertos, its Halloween party.

Three short video posts lead up to the night. La Catrina, the figure already inside Barbossa, introduces the event. The party itself is at Barbossa, built around its reggaeton nights.

Teaser 01 · La Catrina introduces the event

The Invitation

Source

An existing photograph of the La Catrina character inside Barbossa. We animate this photograph with AI so she comes to life and speaks directly to the audience.

  1. The video opens on the still photograph of La Catrina.
  2. AI animation brings her to life: her eyes open, her face moves and she begins to speak.
  3. She delivers the voiceover directly to camera.
  4. When she finishes, the screen fades to black.
  5. The event information appears on black.
Voiceover · La Catrina

Once a year, I return.

They might call it Halloween.

We call it Noche de los Muertos.

Teaser 02 · The ofrenda reveals the celebration

The Ofrenda

Source

An image of a Mexican-inspired ofrenda decorated with candles and marigolds, animated with AI.

  1. The video opens on the ofrenda.
  2. A hand enters the frame.
  3. The hand lights a candle.
  4. As the flame appears, "La ofrenda está lista." appears on screen.
  5. The line disappears.
  6. The event information is revealed.

Teaser 03 · Party footage builds the excitement

The Night Begins

Source

Existing footage from previous reggaeton parties at Barbossa.

  1. A fast, rhythmic edit of real party moments: people dancing, drinks, music and the crowd.
  2. Cut to an upbeat reggaeton track.
  3. The event details appear on screen throughout the video.
  4. It closes on the full event information.

Energetic, sexy and social. This is the most promotional of the three posts and the one that drives attendance.

Social extensions

Flyer designs

Four flyers created from existing Barbossa photography, enhanced with AI. Real women, Catrina-inspired styling and a warm, dark nightlife palette, designed to work together as one campaign.

DJ XXX is a placeholder until the DJ is confirmed.

Visual inspiration

Cultural references for individual details: cempasúchil, candlelight, ofrenda elements and typography.

The campaign itself is led by real women from Barbossa's shoots, with Catrina-inspired styling and a warm, dark palette. These Mexican elements support the visuals rather than lead them.
